notes: Account summary: fintech fraud detection + customer chat + personalized product ranking. Very latency-sensitive for user-facing chat on mobile (low-bandwidth).
Primary ask: Dedicated capacity with guaranteed throughput and explicit SLO definitions for p50/p95/p99. Want measurement alignment for streaming responses vs non-streaming completions.
Key technical constraints: strict EU data residency for payment flows; on-prem routing for subset of customers; TLS termination happens at customer edge (adds ~15-30ms).

SLO nuance discussed: they want client-side perceived latency included in SLO when feature flag 'perceived_latency=true' is on. Redwood must provide both server-side and client-side traceable measurements and a reproducible method to compute p99 corrected for client edge latency.

Suggested approach agreed in workshop: use server-side requestStart -> lastTokenEmitted for server SLOs, and provide 'client-corrected SLO' where clientStart is customer-supplied header; document sampling strategy for full traces vs summary histograms.

Streaming vs non-streaming: for streaming chat they want 'time-to-first-byte (TTFB)' p50/p95 and 'time-to-last-byte (TTLB)' p99. For non-streaming completions they want single completion latency windows. Need to define tokenized vs decoded boundaries (tokenization on server or client).

Measurement specifics to include in SLO doc: 10s warmup exclusion for cold-starts, 5% traffic synthetic canary latency baseline, bucketed histograms with 1ms granularity for 0-200ms and 10ms for >200ms, and separate histograms for regional POPs.
Operational expectations: 99.9% uptime SLA for Dedicated pool, 95th percentile SLO crediting model, automatic fallback to smaller model family at p99 breach (and notification workflow).
Quote from CTO: 'We care about what our customers feel — p95 doesn't cut it for some flows. We need both tails and streaming first-byte guarantees.'
Gating items: legal needs 'SLO appendix' in contract; infra needs final reserved-GPU number before procurement; CISO requires KMS integration proof-of-concept for key wrapping on-prem.
slo_requirements: Chat (streaming): TTFB p50 <= 60ms, TTFB p95 <= 150ms, TTLB p99 <= 450ms (for 8k token sessions) - measure serverStart->firstToken and serverStart->lastToken
Chat (non-streamed): completion latency p50 <= 120ms, p95 <= 280ms, p99 <= 600ms - measure serverTimestampStart->completionSent
Reranking: end-to-end p95 <= 80ms, p99 <= 220ms (batched QPS plan) - include batching latency window in measurement
Client-corrected measurement: accept x-client-start header; compute clientPerceived = clientStart -> lastTokenClientReceived; provide both raw server histograms and client-corrected percentiles

Measurement boundaries: server-side = API gateway ingress -> last byte enqueued to network socket; client-side = client header start -> final byte acknowledged. Streaming first byte recorded as soon as first chunk leaves runtime.
Sampling and telemetry: full traces for 0.1% of requests, histogram summarization for all requests; ensure histograms support p50/p95/p99 computation with correction factors.
capacity_expectations: Baseline: sustained 250 qps (concurrent chat sessions ~3k) with burst buffer to 500 qps for 15 minutes
Reserve recommendation: 6 x V100-equivalent GPUs for baseline + 2x burst pool (auto-burst) - Redwood proposed sizing shared 2026-02-22
KV cache warm fraction target: 85% active during business hours; cold-start tail budgeted in SLO policy
Throughput guarantees: request-level concurrency limits, per-GPU throughput metrics to be exposed to account via Console
commercial_notes: Pricing: prefer annual reserved contract with quarterly true-ups. Want explicit credits if p99 exceeds agreed threshold more than 2x in a month.
Legal asks: SLO appendix with measurement methodology, sample dataset for e2e tests, data residency SLA for EU transactions.
